pages.quiz:
ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only a describing word
   D. Only a joining word

2. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.2 Speaking: Etiquette.

3. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. went
   C. goes
   D. goed

4. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.

5. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Spelling.

6. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. No full stops
   C. One main idea with supporting sentences
   D. Only one word repeated

7. When practising Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening.

8. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.

9. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.

10. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the library

11. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Sentence Fluency.

12. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 4.1.2 Conversational Skills: Speaking Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 4.2.1 Study Skills: Library Skills and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in use 4.3.1 Word Classes and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Phrases and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

3. B — went

4. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency.

6. C — One main idea with supporting sentences

8. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: Verbs Main and Auxiliary Verbs, Tense and Asp.

9. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: fluency in speaking.

12. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word Classes.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 4.1.2 Conversational Skills: Speaking Fluency; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 4.2.1 Study Skills: Library Skills; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in use 4.3.1 Word Classes; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Phrases; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
